name: Deduction for qualified overtime compensation (No Tax on Overtime)
legalBasis: Internal Revenue Code section 225, added by Public Law 119-21 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed July 4, 2025), section 70202
assumptions: Only the FLSA-required premium (the 'half' of time-and-a-half for hours over 40 in a workweek) is qualified overtime compensation. Premiums above what the FLSA requires, and premiums paid only under state law, a union contract or employer policy, do not qualify.
Employees who are exempt from FLSA overtime cannot claim the deduction, even if they receive overtime pay.

The cap applies first; the MAGI reduction is then subtracted from the capped amount (Schedule 1-A, Part III). The reduction is $100 for each full $1,000 of MAGI above the threshold; a partial $1,000 is dropped (Schedule 1-A says to decrease the result to the next lower whole number).

Married people must file a joint return to claim the deduction; married filing separately gets $0. Qualifying surviving spouse and head of household use the $12,500 cap and $150,000 threshold, because only a joint return gets the higher amounts.
A valid Social Security number (valid for employment) must appear on the return.
The deduction reduces federal taxable income only. It does not reduce Social Security or Medicare (FICA) taxes, and state income tax treatment depends on each state.
Estimated savings = deduction x the marginal federal rate the user selects. A large deduction can move part of the income into a lower bracket, so the true saving can be slightly lower.

2025.reportingNote: For 2025, employers were not required to report qualified overtime separately. Notice 2025-69 lets employees use a premium shown on a pay statement or W-2 box 14, one-third of total overtime pay paid at time-and-a-half (one-quarter at double time), or another reasonable method.

2026.reportingNote: From tax year 2026 employers must report qualified overtime separately, most commonly in Form W-2 box 12 with code TT (Form 1099-NEC box 1d or 1099-MISC box 14 for non-employees). Only reported amounts count; if the amount is too low, ask the employer for a corrected W-2. Form 4852 cannot be used to claim unreported overtime.

2027.reportingNote: Same rules as 2026 unless Congress or the IRS changes them. Amounts in section 225 are not indexed for inflation.

2028.reportingNote: 2028 is the last tax year the deduction applies under current law.
